title: Existence of split reductive groups realizing reduced root data
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. A reduced root datum is a free abelian group $M$ of finite rank, a finite subset $R\subset M\setminus\{0\}$, and a bijection $\alpha\mapsto\alpha^\vee$ onto a subset of $M^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z}(M,\mathbf Z)$, such that $\langle\alpha,\alpha^\vee\rangle=2$, each reflection $s_\alpha(m)=m-\langle m,\alpha^\vee\rangle\alpha$ permutes $R$, the group these reflections generate on $M$ is finite, and $\mathbf Q\alpha\cap R=\{\alpha,-\alpha\}$. For every reduced root datum $(M,R,M^\vee,R^\vee)$ there exist a split reductive $F$-group scheme $G$ [def-sc-group-scheme], a split maximal torus $S\subseteq G$, and an isomorphism from its root datum to the prescribed datum, including an identification $X^*(S)\simeq M$ carrying roots and coroots to $R,R^\vee$. Reductive, split maximal torus, characters, cocharacters and the group root datum have the meanings of [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Empty root sets and rank zero are allowed.

source.place: Theorem 23.55, printed p.501; Definition C.28, printed pp.613--614.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-root-datum-lattice-embedding] to the prescribed datum. It gives the rational root system $(V,R)$, its weight lattice $P$, the central lattice $C$, and $j:M\hookrightarrow L=P\oplus C$ with finite cokernel. Put $N=j(M)$. Thus $N$ has finite index in $L$, contains every $(\alpha,0)$, and $\alpha^\vee(m)=\bar c_\alpha(\pi_Vm)$. This retains the central directions, even when the roots do not span $M\otimes\mathbf Q$.

source.place: Appendix C.29, C.35, C.43--C.44, pp.614--618; rational form of the reduction in Exercise 21-4, p.461.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-chevalley-admissible-representation] for $(V,R)$. Choose its rational Lie algebra, faithful representation $\rho$ on $W$, and integral lattice $\Lambda$. In particular the weights generate the full lattice $P$, the lattice splits into its weight sublattices, and every $D_{\alpha,m}=\rho(e_\alpha)^m/m!$ is integral and is zero for all sufficiently large $m$. All the hypotheses for the root-exponential construction are therefore available, over the given $F$ in any characteristic.

source.place: Section 23h, pp.503--510; full-weight choice in Corollary 23.73, p.511.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-chevalley-root-exponential-group] to these data and $F$. On $\Lambda\otimes F$ form $x_\alpha(a)=\sum_m(D_{\alpha,m}\otimes1)a^m$. Here reduction to $F$ is applied to the integral matrices, so no factorial is inverted in $F$. The subgroup they generate is the split semisimple group $H$ with maximal torus $T_H=D_F(P)$ and root datum $(P,R,\bar c_\alpha)$. This supplies an actual group before any isogeny or quotient is considered.

Apply [lem-sfb-central-character-sublattice-quotient] to $H$, $C$ and $N\subseteq P\oplus C$. The needed finite index and inclusion of all $(\alpha,0)$ were verified in step 1. It constructs the finite central subgroup $K=D_F((P\oplus C)/N)$ of $H\times D_F(C)$ and the split reductive quotient $G=(H\times D_F(C))/K$. Its split maximal torus $S$ has character lattice $N$, roots $(\alpha,0)$, and coroots $n\mapsto\bar c_\alpha(\operatorname{pr}_P n)$. This use includes nonreduced $K$; no separability assumption on the quotient of tori is made.

Identify $X^*(S)=N$ with $M$ by $j^{-1}$. Each root $(\alpha,0)=j(\alpha)$ is carried to $\alpha$. For every $m\in M$ the constructed coroot evaluates on $j(m)$ as $\bar c_\alpha(\operatorname{pr}_P j(m))=\bar c_\alpha(\pi_Vm)=\alpha^\vee(m)$. Hence the dual identification also carries every coroot to the prescribed one, and this is an isomorphism of the full root data. For $R=\varnothing$ the cited constructions give $V=P=0$, $C=M$, $j$ an isomorphism, $H=K=1$ and $G=D_F(M)$. For $M=0$ this is the trivial group. Thus neither edge case needs an additional hypothesis.
